items.title: Nonnegative test supermartingales
items.statement: Assuming AC, on a common discrete filtered probability space and for a null family of laws P0, an adapted, integrable process E_t that is nonnegative P-almost surely at every time, is a supermartingale under every P in P0, and satisfies E_P E_0 <= 1 for every P in P0 is a nonnegative test supermartingale for P0. Time starts at zero.

items.title: Ville's inequality for nonnegative test supermartingales
items.statement: Assume AC. For every P in P0, every nonnegative test supermartingale E under P, and every alpha in (0,1), P(sup_{t>=0} E_t >= 1/alpha) <= alpha.
items.strategy: For any gamma, bound the actual first threshold hit using tau_gamma truncated at N, bounded optional sampling, nonnegativity, and continuity from below. For the supremum statement, if its probability q exceeds alpha, use beta=(alpha+q)/2 and the lower-threshold hit bound to contradict q>alpha.

items.title: Mixtures of null test supermartingales
items.statement: Assume AC. Let pi be a probability measure on a measurable space Lambda. If (lambda,omega) maps to E_t^lambda(omega) is measurable with respect to A tensor F_t for every t and each E^lambda is a nonnegative test supermartingale for the same null family P0, then its pi-mixture, with an everywhere-finite version chosen by setting the mixture to zero where its integral is infinite, is a nonnegative test supermartingale for P0.
items.strategy: Tonelli gives adaptedness and integrability of the mixture. Test the conditional-supermartingale inequality on every event in F_{t-1}, integrate the component inequalities, and use the event-integral characterization of conditional expectation.

items.title: Anytime-valid p-value processes
items.statement: On a common discrete filtered probability space and for a null family P0, an adapted process p_t with values in [0,1] is an anytime-valid p-value process if for every P in P0 and alpha in (0,1), P(exists t>=0: p_t <= alpha) <= alpha. For each threshold alpha, the rejection rule 1{p_t <= alpha} is an F_t-measurable deterministic test via its binary probability kernel; every finite stopping-time rejection event is contained in the all-times crossing event.

items.title: A test supermartingale gives anytime-valid p-values
items.statement: Assume AC. If E is a nonnegative test supermartingale for P0, define p_t=1 when E_t<=0 and p_t=min(1,1/E_t) otherwise. Then p is an anytime-valid p-value process for P0; for every P in P0, fixed t>=0 and u in [0,1], P(p_t<=u)<=u. For every possibly unbounded stopping time tau and u in [0,1], P(tau<infinity, p_tau<=u)<=u under every P in P0.
items.strategy: The Borel transform handles every real version of E_t. For alpha in (0,1), the all-times p-value crossing equals the actual evidence-hit event, which is contained in Ville's supremum event. Prove fixed-time and stopping-time bounds by inclusion, check endpoints, and identify p_t as a valid p-value in the nonempty fixed-time experiment.

items.title: Confidence sequences
items.statement: For a parameter family (P_theta) on a common discrete filtered probability space, a (1-alpha) confidence sequence is a sequence of set-valued rules C_t such that each fixed-parameter membership event {theta in C_t} is F_t-measurable and P_theta(theta in C_t for every t>=0) >= 1-alpha.

items.title: Confidence sequences by test-supermartingale inversion
items.statement: Assume AC and alpha in (0,1). Let (P_theta) be a parameter-indexed family on a common discrete filtered space. If for each theta, E_t^theta is a nonnegative test supermartingale for the singleton null {P_theta}, then C_t={theta:E_t^theta<1/alpha} is a (1-alpha) confidence sequence.
items.strategy: For each fixed theta, transform E^theta to its anytime-valid p-value process. The event that theta is ever excluded is exactly the p-value crossing event and therefore has probability at most alpha.

title: Sequential Validity and Ville's Inequality — Examples

items.title: A finite-horizon likelihood-ratio test supermartingale
items.statement: On Omega={0,1}^K with the uniform law P0 and its prefix filtration, let Q be the product Bernoulli(3/4) law and P0 the product Bernoulli(1/2) law. The likelihood ratio E_t=dQ|F_t/dP0|F_t, held constant after K, is a nonnegative test martingale under P0 and hence a test supermartingale.
items.strategy: Compute the one-step likelihood ratio values, check their conditional mean on each prefix atom, and verify the finite-horizon process is adapted, integrable, nonnegative, and starts at one.

items.title: A data-dependent threshold crossing
items.statement: For two fair coin observations and the likelihood-ratio process from Bernoulli(3/4) against Bernoulli(1/2), the stopping rule tau=inf{t>=0:E_t>=2} rejects only on two heads, an event of probability 1/4 under the null. The level-1/2 threshold is selected from the data through the first-crossing rule, and the finite-horizon crossing probability is at most 1/2.
items.strategy: Compute E_0,E_1,E_2 on all four outcomes, identify the first-crossing event, and compare its probability with the Ville bound at alpha=1/2.

items.title: Validity under one null law does not give a composite-null test supermartingale
items.statement: Let X be Bernoulli(1/4) or Bernoulli(3/4) under two null laws, take F_0 trivial, F_t=sigma(X) for t>=1, M_0=1, and M_t=2X for t>=1. M is a nonnegative supermartingale under Bernoulli(1/4), but not under Bernoulli(3/4), so it is not a test supermartingale for the composite null family.
items.strategy: Compute the conditional mean at time one under each null law. The first satisfies the supermartingale inequality and the second violates it.
